subject: Request: Tailored remediation package & one-time credit for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Aisha Khatri <aisha.khatri@nimbushealth.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: Nimbus Health Billing <billing@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T08:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: service disruption impact and next steps

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the postmortem — we reviewed the attached PDF and the impact window on 2028-05-15 caused our nightly ingestion jobs to miss two critical windows. That resulted in delays for several downstream reports and an SLA credit request from our finance team.

We need a clear remediation package and a one-time credit to present to our CFO. Specifically:
- A fixed credit covering the missed SLA for May (line-item on invoice)
- A short remediation runway (2 weeks) with a named owner and rollback plan
- Evidence that the fix will not degrade latency for our high-priority routes

Can Redwood propose something by EOD so we can close the internal ticket? Samir from our procurement/legal is copied for contract language.

Thanks,
Aisha
Senior Ops Lead, Nimbus Health

Attachments: postmortem-nimbus-20280515.pdf

From: chloe_martin@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, aisha.khatri@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2028-05-16T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: service disruption impact and next steps

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Nimbus's ask. Summary: May 15th incident created a billing/finance escalation. They want a one-time credit, a two-week remediation plan with named owners, and assurances about latency.

Quick context:
- Root cause: autoscaler race condition on dedicated pools during a burst; KV cache thrash amplified tail latency for a subset of tenants (see attached postmortem).
- Impact: ~3 hours of increased P95 on a particular routing path affecting their nightly jobs. Not a full outage, but enough for their SLA threshold to trigger.

Suggested immediate offer to close fast:
1) One-time invoice credit equal to 50% of May usage for routes affected (roughly $16,000) — refundable credit applied to next invoice.
2) Two-week remediation sprint led by Jonas (ops) + a latency monitoring doc and customer-facing runbook.
3) Optional 1-month complimentary pro-rate of Dedicated buffer for burst protection while we stabilize.

I asked Jonas to draft the term sheet; see the attached proposed-remediation-term-sheet.xlsx. They want a decision today to present to their CFO.

Karthik — can you advise whether we should escalate to Exec for signoff or if we can approve under delegated concession authority? Marissa, if you OK the above, would appreciate a one-line signoff I can forward.

Thanks,
Chloe
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, aisha.khatri@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2028-05-16T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: service disruption impact and next steps

Marissa — tagging you for exec authorization. This is a mid-market account on a growing plan; we want to preserve the expansion motion but also be judicious with concessions. Proposed package (same as Chloe):
- One-time credit: $16k (approx 50% of affected line)
- Two-week remediation sprint with named SLA owner (Jonas)
- 1-month pro-rated buffer (no-cost) as a goodwill gesture

Rationale: keeps the account stable, prevents finance churn, and avoids legal friction. If we can approve up to $20k in total concessions under delegated authority, we keep this out of a formal executive approval loop. If more than $20k, we should escalate.

About the credit accounting: we'll book as a service credit against the May invoice; finance is copied on the HubSpot note linked here: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/record/987654

Can you confirm whether to proceed within the $20k delegation or escalate to the Exec committee?

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Sales Operations

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: aisha.khatri@nimbushealth.com, samir.patel@velocity-legal.com
Date: 2028-05-16T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: service disruption impact and next steps

Chloe / Karthik — I reviewed the impact and the proposed remediation term sheet. I approve the following, effective immediately:

- One-time credit capped at $18,000 to be applied to the next invoice (Finance to implement).
- Two-week remediation sprint led by Jonas Weber (Ops). Jonas, please provide a daily stand-up note and a customer-facing runbook by EOD tomorrow.
- One-month pro-rated Dedicated buffer to be enabled at no charge; operations to confirm safe rollback paths.

Conditions:
- The credit approval is a one-time gesture tied to the attached postmortem and the proposed remediation plan. Any follow-on requests for additional credits or contract changes must go through Exec review.
- Legal to approve the final concession language; Samir, please coordinate with our counsel on the short addendum.

Chloe — please send a succinct approval email to Aisha with the bullets above and attach the term sheet. Keep the tone conciliatory and clear on conditions.

Marissa
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
